stumbles.quote: Interference colours match a reference to mean ΔE76 0.07.
stumbles.why: The reference is never identified (a photo? a physical model?), so I can't tell what the colours are being compared to. The metric is also unexplained, and 0.07 is so small that it's hard to believe without knowing what was measured.

stumbles.quote: thick film sinks the way you tilt the phone, thin film rises
stumbles.why: This is ambiguous. I can't tell whether thick film sinks toward the low side of the tilt, or whether 'the way you tilt' means something else. It also needs a phone's tilt sensor, but the post says it hasn't been tested on a phone.

stumbles.quote: Checked headless on a software GPU, not yet on a phone.
stumbles.why: It's unclear what was actually verified. Colour match and simulation may have been checked, but tilt can't have been. It's also unclear whether the demo needs WebGPU support that phones may lack.

point: A WebGPU compute soap-film demo where film thickness acts as density, so thick film sinks and thin film rises as you tilt the phone. Its interference colours were checked against a reference, but only on a software GPU and not yet on a phone.
